summary: Jordan Whitfield led a pricing and packaging review with James Mitchell (sales), Diana Reeves (Customer Success) and Marcus Williams (billing support) ahead of the Q3 price book lock. Marcus reported nine Comply overage disputes since the v2 launch, mostly caused by customers exploring on-demand reports without usage warnings, while James noted that SentinelShield and VaultEdge quote simpler flat pricing. Diana and Jordan raised concern that free year-one Comply discounts used to save renewals will create a second wave of overage disputes. The team agreed to propose three Comply tiers with unlimited on-demand reports, credits for overages charged since April 7, an in-console usage page and 80% seat alerts, accepting ~$110K in lost overage revenue that finance expects to recover through higher Professional-tier deals bundled with Protect. Protect bundle onboardings will be gated on the scheduler rollout.
